questions.prompt: According to the listening passage, when did education begin?
steps: The passage places learning at the beginning of human life, before books or formal schools.
Select the earliest event named in the options.
questions.answer: B — When human beings were created.

questions.prompt: What helps a person become self-reliant and self-aware?
steps: Identify the tool linked to independence and awareness in the passage.
The answer is the state of having received education.

questions.prompt: What two categories of education are described?
steps: Separate learning through ordinary family life from structured schooling.
The passage contrasts these two kinds rather than individual activities.

questions.prompt: What education should young people receive to create well-educated citizens?
steps: The question seeks the broad preparation described in the passage.
Include learning both inside and outside formal institutions.
questions.answer: D — Both formal and informal education.

questions.prompt: What basic benefit did formal education bring?
steps: Recall the three elementary skills named for the new schooling.
They concern literacy and numeracy.

questions.prompt: I ___ practise cooking next Saturday.
steps: Next Saturday refers to the future.
Use will + base verb to express the planned future action.

questions.prompt: He used to ___ sports programmes.
steps: Used to is followed by the base form of a verb.
The required base form is watch.

questions.prompt: The train ___ late three times this week.
steps: This week is an unfinished period, so the present perfect fits repeated events.
The train is singular: use has + past participle been.

questions.prompt: Mussa and Abdul ___ tennis now.
steps: Now indicates an action in progress.
With a plural subject, use are + playing.

questions.prompt: Our former teacher ___ us happy during his classes.
steps: The account concerns a former teacher’s past behaviour.
The simple past of keep is kept.

questions.prompt: Rajabu and Paul were mopping ___ their sister was washing dishes.
steps: The two activities happened at the same time.
While links simultaneous actions.

questions.prompt: Janeth went to school ___ foot.
steps: The fixed expression for walking as transport is on foot.
By is used with many vehicles, but not in this expression.

questions.prompt: Bats are more active ___ night.
steps: The standard expression is at night.
Use at for this time phrase.

questions.prompt: The man was sentenced to two years ___ jail.
steps: The sentence describes being inside prison.
The established phrase is in jail.

questions.prompt: The thief jumped ___ the gate.
steps: The movement goes across the top of an obstacle.
Over expresses that crossing.

questions.prompt: The beast was not only ugly ___ dirty.
steps: Complete the paired structure not only … but also.
Both adjectives add information about the same beast.

questions.prompt: ___ I won’t be able to attend the birthday party.
steps: Choose a polite introductory expression for unwelcome information.
I am afraid softens the refusal.

questions.prompt: Neither John ___ Mary sat for the mock examination.
steps: The negative pair is neither … nor.
Or belongs to either … or instead.

questions.prompt: Change He said that he was watering the flowers into direct speech.
steps: Restore the speaker’s own pronoun I.
In the usual reported-speech conversion, was watering is the backshift of am watering.
questions.answer: C — He said, “I am watering the flowers.”

questions.prompt: Add a question tag: He is a Standard Seven pupil.
steps: A positive statement takes a negative tag.
Repeat the auxiliary is and subject he: isn’t he?

questions.prompt: Reply positively to Excuse me, sir, may I come in?
steps: May asks for permission.
Grant permission with the same auxiliary: Yes, you may.

questions.prompt: We prefer eating rice ___ potatoes.
steps: Use the construction prefer X to Y.
To introduces the less-preferred alternative.

questions.prompt: Children without a balanced diet become ___.
steps: The context describes a harmful consequence.
Add un- to healthy to form the appropriate opposite.

questions.prompt: Cooks who are ___ have many burn marks.
steps: After are, an adjective describes the cooks.
Careless means not taking enough care; it fits the stated accidents.

questions.prompt: Nina is the ___ of the two intelligent girls.
steps: A comparison of two people uses a comparative.
For intelligent, form the comparative with more.

questions.prompt: Breaking off a relationship means deciding to ___ it.
steps: Break off means discontinue something.
The matching verb is end.

questions.prompt: What word is closest to instructions?
steps: Instructions tell someone what to do and how to do it.
Directions is the closest word in this context.

questions.prompt: Give the opposite of clean.
steps: Clean means free from dirt.
Its direct opposite is dirty.

questions.prompt: A chameleon does not move fast; it walks ___.
steps: The blank describes how the animal walks, so use an adverb.
The opposite of quickly is slowly.

questions.prompt: Bad pupils ___ their teachers, unlike good pupils who respect them.
steps: Choose a verb opposite in meaning to respect.
Disrespect means fail to show respect.

questions.prompt: At her birthday celebration, my sister has dressed ___.
steps: The blank describes the manner of dressing.
Smartly is the adverb expressing a neat appearance.

questions.prompt: There are ___ oranges left in the fridge.
steps: Oranges is a plural countable noun.
Few is used with plural countable things and is the intended quantifier here.
questions.tip: More can also form a grammatical sentence in a comparison context, but few is NECTA’s expected answer for this item.

questions.prompt: A farmer tills the soil using ___.
steps: Tilling means loosening and turning the soil.
A hoe is the agricultural tool intended in the options.

questions.prompt: Besides jewellery, ring can refer to the sound of what?
steps: Ring has more than one meaning.
A bell rings; its ringing sound is also called a ring.

questions.prompt: Kaunda cut ___ with a knife.
steps: The subject and injured person are the same male person.
Use the reflexive pronoun himself.

questions.prompt: Order the sentence: At the end, each team had one goal.
steps: Introduce the match before recounting its goals.
The phrase at the end concludes the composition, so this sentence is fifth.

questions.prompt: Order the sentence: Dogo boys scored first in the first half.
steps: The match introduction comes first.
The first goal is the next event, before the equalising goal.

questions.prompt: Order the sentence: There was a match between Dogo boys and Goma boys.
steps: A composition first introduces the event and participants.
This sentence supplies that opening information.

questions.prompt: Order the sentence: Both teams played tirelessly as time was nearly over.
steps: This happens after the first-half goal and second-half equaliser.
It precedes the final result.

questions.prompt: Order the sentence: Goma boys equalised in the second half.
steps: The first-half goal must come before the second-half equaliser.
This is followed by the final effort and result.

questions.prompt: What was Mr Kikuko’s occupation?
steps: The passage says he made furniture.
A person who makes furniture from wood is a carpenter.

questions.prompt: Why did Mbuto engage in child labour?
steps: His father died and his mother could no longer work.
He was the eldest child and had to seek money for the household.
questions.answer: He worked to support his family after his father died and his mother became too ill to work.

questions.prompt: Why did Mbuto cry after breaking his leg?
steps: Look beyond physical pain to the fear stated in the passage.
He knew the injury could prevent him from providing for his family.
questions.answer: He was in pain and feared he could no longer support his family.

questions.prompt: Why did Mbuto work in the mine instead of attending school?
steps: He had left school to earn a living for his family.
Selling on the street did not provide enough money, so he sought paid work at the mine.
questions.answer: His family needed income, and street sales were insufficient, so he took a mining job.

questions.prompt: What enabled Mbuto to return to school?
steps: Identify the person who offered help after his injury.
A nurse promised to care for his family and arrange his return to education.
questions.answer: A nurse’s support for his family enabled him to return to school.

summaries.Section A — Listening: Record the main idea and key contrasts while listening. Answer from the passage, rather than guessing from an option that sounds reasonable.
summaries.Section A — Grammar and vocabulary: Notice tense markers, subject agreement and fixed expressions. Check whether the blank requires a verb, adjective, adverb or pronoun.
summaries.Section B — Composition: The complete order is 38 → 37 → 40 → 39 → 36: introduction, first goal, equaliser, final effort, result.
summaries.Section C — Comprehension: Use facts from the passage and answer the exact question. Causes, motives and consequences may require different sentences.
